In addition to amending the Form 144 filing deadline, we are making two technical amendments. First, we are amending three provisions to correct errors about the time period during which filings made by direct submission may be submitted to the Commission. In particular, we are correcting errors in 17 CFR 230.110(c) (“Rule 110” under the Securities Act), 240.0-2(c) (“Rule 0-2(c)” under the Exchange Act), and 260.0-5(c) (“Rule 0-5(c)” under the Trust Indenture Act) by conforming them to 17 CFR 232.12(c) (“Rule 12(c)” of Regulation S-T) and Section 2.3.1 of the EDGAR Filer Manual.[18]
Rules 110(c), 0-2(c), and 0-5(c) currently provide that filings made by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission each business day, from “8 a.m. to 10 p.m.” In fact, filings may be submitted starting at 6 a.m. Consequently, we are revising Rules 110(c), 0-2(c), and 0-5(c) to replace “8 a.m.” with “6 a.m.”
Second, we are reinstating the Regulation S-T-based requirement for paper filings of Form 144 for non-reporting issuers that was inadvertently removed in the Electronic Filing Release.[19]

# Regulatory extract and reconciliation — 17 CFR § 240.0-2(c) (Business hours of the Commission; electronic filings)

**Basis of preparation.** This memo reproduces regulatory text as it appears on the fetched source pages and reconciles the reproductions against each other. Period/version: CFR Title 17, Volume 4, print date 2025-04-01, plus the eCFR 'current' page retrieved 2026-11-23 and Federal Register 88 FR 12209 (Feb. 27, 2023). Currency: USD is irrelevant here — no monetary amounts are stated; the only computed quantities are elapsed times. Basis: verbatim text, not paraphrase, with each figure's source and arithmetic shown. Draft for review by a qualified compliance or finance professional; compliance information, not legal advice.

---

## 1. The answer, verbatim

> **(c) Electronic filings.** Filings made by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect.

Source: 17 CFR § 240.0-2(c), as reproduced at https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title17-vol4/xhtml/CFR-2025-title17-vol4-sec240-0-2.html (CFR Title 17, Vol. 4, date 2025-04-01; fetched 2026-11-23, sha256 038795da7cb0). Source note printed with the section: `[58 FR 14682, Mar. 18, 1993, as amended at 65 FR 24801, Apr. 27, 2000; 68 FR 25799, May 13, 2003; 73 FR 973, Jan. 4, 2008; 88 FR 12209, Feb. 27, 2023]`.

## 2. The two requested values, itemised

### 2.1 Daily submission window (on days when direct-transmission filings are accepted)

**6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect** — i.e. Washington, DC local clock time. The rule itself performs no time-zone conversion; a filer outside Eastern Time converts.

Arithmetic on the window:
- 10:00 p.m. = 22:00; 6:00 a.m. = 06:00.
- 22:00 − 06:00 = **16 hours = 960 minutes**.
- DST caveat, stated precisely: the window is defined in wall-clock terms, so on the spring-forward day elapsed time is 15 h and on the fall-back day 17 h. Both transitions fall on a Sunday (second Sunday in March; first Sunday in November), and Sunday is an excluded day under this same subsection, so **no open day ever carries a non-16-hour window**. The 16-hour figure therefore holds for every day on which filings are accepted.

### 2.2 Days excluded

**Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays** — exactly three categories, as named in the text. Nothing else is excluded by the text of § 240.0-2(c). In particular, the text does **not** name: state or local holidays, days the Commission's offices close for weather or emergency, or EDGAR system-unavailability days. Those may affect operations but are not excluded days on the face of this subsection.

## 3. Version control — the one way this answer goes wrong

The window changed. The Federal Register document adopting the current text states:

> "Rules 110(c), 0-2(c), and 0-5(c) currently provide that filings made by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission each business day, from '8 a.m. to 10 p.m.' In fact, filings may be submitted starting at 6 a.m. Consequently, we are revising Rules 110(c), 0-2(c), and 0-5(c) to replace '8 a.m.' with '6 a.m.'"
> — https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/html/2023/02/27/2023-03931.html (fetched 2026-11-23, sha256 f2abe034cd7a)

and gives the effective date:

> "We therefore find there is good cause for these amendments to take effect on March 20, 2023." — same source.

| Attribute | Superseded text (before Mar. 20, 2023) | Current text (Mar. 20, 2023 →) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Start of window | 8 a.m. (per FR description of prior text) | **6 a.m.** | Current = 6 a.m.; 8 a.m. is stale |
| End of window | 10 p.m. | 10 p.m. | Unchanged |
| Day qualifier | "each business day" (per FR description of prior text) | "each day" | Substantively same set of days, since the exclusion clause is identical |
| Excluded days | Saturdays, Sundays, Federal holidays | Saturdays, Sundays, Federal holidays | Unchanged |

**Reviewer test:** if the page you are working from shows "8 a.m.", it reproduces a pre-March 20, 2023 text and must not be used. The current operative start time is 6 a.m. The "business day" → "day" wording change does not alter the excluded-day list, because both formulations carve out Saturdays, Sundays and Federal holidays.

## 4. Cross-check of reproductions (reconciliation)

| # | Source | Start | End | Excluded days |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | govinfo CFR 2025, xhtml (sha256 038795da7cb0) | 6 a.m. | 10 p.m. | Sat, Sun, Federal holidays |
| 2 | govinfo CFR 2025, PDF (sha256 7168a522b2dd) | 6 a.m. | 10 p.m. | Sat, Sun, Federal holidays |
| 3 | govinfo CFR 2025, XML (sha256 7fa19039094a) | 6 a.m. | 10 p.m. | Sat, Sun, Federal holidays |
| 4 | eCFR current § 240.0-2 (sha256 f86928af7bf9) | 6 a.m. | 10 p.m. | Sat, Sun, Federal holidays |
| 5 | FR 88 FR 12209, amendatory instruction No. 10 (sha256 f2abe034cd7a) | 6 a.m. | 10 p.m. | Sat, Sun, Federal holidays |
| 6 | Parallel Rule 232.12(c), eCFR Part 232 (sha256 bbe7e989641a) | 6 a.m. | 10 p.m. | Sat, Sun, Federal holidays |

Agreement: 6 of 6 on start time, 6 of 6 on end time, 6 of 6 on the excluded-day list. **Variance: 0.** No figure in this memo is unsupported by at least three of these entries.

## 5. The window is not the filing deadline — do not conflate them

The 16-hour window is the period in which a direct transmission may be *submitted*. Whether a submission is *timely* or *deemed filed* on a given business day is governed separately, principally by 17 CFR § 232.13. The fetched Federal Register page quotes:

> "No later than 5:30 p.m., will be deemed filed on the same business day; and" … "After 5:30 p.m., will be deemed filed the next business day."

with an exception:

> "a Form 3, 4, or 5 or Schedule 14N submitted by direct transmission on or before 10:00 p.m. will be deemed filed on the same business day."

Consequence, with arithmetic:
- 06:00 → 17:30 = 11.5 hours = 690 minutes of the window that is inside the ordinary same-day deemed-filing cutoff.
- 17:30 → 22:00 = 4.5 hours = 270 minutes of the window that, for ordinary filings, rolls to the next business day.
- 690 + 270 = 960 minutes = 16 hours — ties to §2.1.
- For Forms 3, 4, 5 and Schedule 14N, the deemed-filing cutoff (10:00 p.m.) coincides with the end of the submission window (10:00 p.m.); the two are equal, and the memo does not assert that either extends past the other.
- **Grounding caveat:** § 232.13 is quoted here only from the Federal Register excerpt, not from a fetched full text of § 232.13. Confirm the deemed-filing cutoffs against the current eCFR text of § 232.13 before relying on them for a specific filing.

## 6. Assumptions, limits and items a reviewer must confirm

1. **"The cited page."** The request refers to a page that was not attached. The answer above is read from the CFR/eCFR/FR reproductions listed in §4, which agree verbatim on every operative word. If the reviewer's page shows different wording, §3 tells you which version you are holding.
2. **"Federal holidays" is not defined in § 240.0-2.** The operative reference is the federal holidays observed in the District of Columbia (5 U.S.C. 6103). This is an assumption imported from outside the subsection, flagged as such.
3. **Emergency/weather closures** of the Commission or EDGAR are not named in § 240.0-2(c) and are therefore not excluded days on the face of the rule, even though they may suspend acceptance in fact. EDGAR operational notices, not this section, govern those.
4. **Time zone.** Times are EST or EDT as in effect in Washington, DC, per the text itself; no conversion is performed by the rule.
5. **Currency of text.** The eCFR 'current' page retrieved 2026-11-23 matched the 2025-04-01 CFR print with no later amendment shown for § 240.0-2(c). Re-verify at the time of any filing; this is a time-sensitive citation.
6. **Scope.** Compliance information for professional review; not legal, tax or investment advice, and not filing advice for a specific filer or a specific form.

## 7. Bottom line for the filer

On any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or Federal holiday, a filing by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission between **6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Eastern Time** (EST or EDT as then in effect). Those three day-categories — Saturdays, Sundays and Federal holidays — are the only exclusions stated in § 240.0-2(c). Being inside the window does not by itself make a filing same-day for deemed-filing purposes; the 5:30 p.m. cutoff (with the 10:00 p.m. carve-out for Forms 3, 4, 5 and Schedule 14N) does that.

verdict.summary:
12 CFR Part 329 — Level 2A and Level 2B liquid asset amounts

Period: as of the calculation date. The prompt does not specify the calendar date.
Currency: US dollars (USD).
Basis: fair value of assets asserted to be eligible HQLA; no other caps or adjustments applied; no level 1 assets are provided or computed.

Source text relied on (12 CFR 329.21(b), as reproduced at https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-329/section-329.21 and https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2026-title12-vol5/pdf/CFR-2026-title12-vol5-part329.pdf):
- 329.21(b)(2): "The level 2A liquid asset amount equals 85 percent of the fair value of all level 2A liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA."
- 329.21(b)(3): "The level 2B liquid asset amount equals 50 percent of the fair value of all level 2B liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA."

Regulatory factors:
- Level 2A factor = 85% = 0.85. This is equivalent to a 15% haircut/deduction from fair value.
- Level 2B factor = 50% = 0.50. This is equivalent to a 50% haircut/deduction from fair value.

Calculation table (USD):
| Class | Fair value input | Regulatory factor | Liquid asset amount = fair value × factor | Deduction = fair value − liquid asset amount |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Level 2A | 80,000,000 | 0.85 | 80,000,000 × 0.85 = 68,000,000 | 80,000,000 − 68,000,000 = 12,000,000 |
| Level 2B | 30,000,000 | 0.50 | 30,000,000 × 0.50 = 15,000,000 | 30,000,000 − 15,000,000 = 15,000,000 |

In USD millions: 80 × 0.85 = 68; 30 × 0.50 = 15.

Sum of the two liquid asset amounts:
68,000,000 + 15,000,000 = 83,000,000 USD.
Cross-check via deductions: total fair value 80,000,000 + 30,000,000 = 110,000,000; total deductions 12,000,000 + 15,000,000 = 27,000,000; 110,000,000 − 27,000,000 = 83,000,000 USD.

Treatment of caps and adjustments:
Per the instruction to ignore other caps and adjustments, I do not apply 329.21(c)-(e) (level 2 cap excess and level 2B cap excess) or 329.21(f)-(i) (adjusted liquid asset amounts and adjusted excess HQLA amount). Accordingly, the amounts above are the un-capped 329.21(b)(2)-(3) liquid asset amounts only. They are not the institution's total HQLA amount under 329.21(a), because that calculation would also require level 1 liquid assets and subtraction of the greater of the unadjusted and adjusted excess HQLA amounts.

Conclusion:
- Level 2A liquid asset amount: $68,000,000.
- Level 2B liquid asset amount: $15,000,000.
- Sum of the level 2A and level 2B liquid asset amounts: $83,000,000.

This is a draft calculation for review by a qualified finance or accounting professional and is not financial, tax, or investment advice.
